nodes.summary: There is a natural number $M \ge 5$ such that every integer Büchi sequence of length $M$ is trivial: for every sequence of integers $u_0, u_1, u_2, \dots$ with $u_{j+2}^2 - 2u_{j+1}^2 + u_j^2 = 2$ for all $j$ with $j + 2 < M$, there is an integer $x$ with $u_j^2 = (x + j)^2$ for all $j < M$.
nodes.title: Resolution of Büchi's square-sequence conjecture

nodes.summary: There is a natural number $M \ge 5$ such that every integer Büchi sequence of length $M$ is trivial: for every sequence of integers $u_0, u_1, u_2, \dots$ with $u_{j+2}^2 - 2u_{j+1}^2 + u_j^2 = 2$ for all $j$ with $j + 2 < M$, there is an integer $x$ with $u_j^2 = (x + j)^2$ for all $j < M$.
nodes.title: Büchi's square-sequence conjecture

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a natural number. A sequence of integers $u_0, u_1, u_2, \dots$ is a Büchi sequence of length $M$ when the second differences of its squares equal $2$ along its first $M$ terms, that is, $u_{j+2}^2 - 2u_{j+1}^2 + u_j^2 = 2$ for every $j$ with $j + 2 < M$.
nodes.title: Büchi sequences

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a natural number. A sequence of integers $u_0, u_1, u_2, \dots$ is trivial at length $M$ when there is an integer $x$ with $u_j^2 = (x + j)^2$ for every $j < M$; equivalently, after changing the signs of some of its terms, its first $M$ terms are the consecutive integers $x, x + 1, \dots, x + M - 1$.
nodes.title: Trivial sequences in Büchi's problem
